## Mandatory workflow for EVERY task

1. Inspect current source, applicable AGENTS.md, Git status, and existing work before starting. Preserve unrelated changes. Use a separate task branch under repository conventions.
2. Reproduce the issue and record the current commit. Implement the smallest coherent fix and meaningful regression coverage. Recheck earlier findings because other work may already have fixed them.
3. **Before EVERY push, typecheck, lint, build, and tests must ALL pass for every affected application/package.** Run checks on the final code being pushed. If code changes afterward, rerun affected checks. A failure, missing script, skipped test, or unverified build is not a pass. Do not push with a known failing gate.
4. Include applicable extra checks: migration validation/integration tests for database work; browser/E2E tests for critical journeys; visual/contrast/keyboard checks for UI changes; Terraform validation/security checks and a reviewed plan for infrastructure changes; secret scanning for all changes. A documentation task must at least pass Markdown/link/secret validation and must not invent successful application checks. Any genuinely inapplicable check needs an explicit reason in the task record.
5. Shared/API changes must also pass checks in all affected consumers. Run against isolated test services and disposable data. Never point mutation, reset, E2E, or load tests at production by default.
6. Record actual commands, exit outcomes, test counts, screenshots where relevant, commit, branch, and remaining limitations. Update this file and the existing completion tracker after verification. Mark separate states: implemented, validated, merged, deployed, and live-verified.
7. Follow repository commit/push conventions. A push that triggers production is a deployment: migration, smoke-test, and recovery prerequisites must be ready. Do not merge, release, rotate credentials, or change infrastructure merely because a planning checkbox exists.

### Required command gates

| Repository | Before-push gate |
| --- | --- |
| Frontend | `yarn check`; UI changes also require `yarn check:ui` (contrast, browser/accessibility/screenshots) |
| Backend | `pnpm check` against an explicitly isolated local test database; migration work additionally requires replay/upgrade checks |
| Mobile | `yarn check` includes all-platform JS export; native builds/device tests follow the change matrix in QUALITY_GATES.md |
| Shared | `yarn check` includes build, direct tests and strict consumer-declaration compilation; API/runtime changes also validate affected apps |
| Infrastructure | `npm run check` includes Terraform validation after real package builds; resource/provider changes additionally need a reviewed plan |

**CG-001 completed:** every repository exposes typecheck, non-writing format/lint, build and tests, enforced in CI and pre-push. Expo JS export does not prove native compilation; see the explicit platform matrix in the mobile quality guide. Store submission is not a test.

## Frontend diagnosis and design decision

**Recommendation: keep React, MUI, React Hook Form, and routing. Replace the conflicting styling layer and inconsistent primitives incrementally.** A Tailwind/shadcn/full-framework migration would add work without automatically correcting contrast, spacing, semantics, or global CSS leakage. Use a configured MUI theme and small app-owned Button, TextField, Select, Card, and PageContainer components. Keep a specialized third-party control only if it meets the same theme, accessibility, and sizing contract.

Target: a modern, quiet marketplace interface with neutral surfaces, readable dark text, a controlled purple primary action, student/employer accents, consistent cards and typography, generous but compact spacing, and predictable mobile layouts. Preserve Croatian copy, brand assets, role identity, and working behavior unless a story explicitly changes them. Bright brand colors can remain decorative; do not assume they work behind white text.

### Historical styling diagnosis — initial audit, now repaired by the FE stories

| Initial evidence | Cause at the initial audit | Repair story |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dark-gray navigation labels on purple filled controls | Global `button` styles in App.css leak into `.main-nav-link`, which has no neutral background/padding reset | FE-002, FE-005 |
| Forgot-password link looks like a large purple CTA beside login | It is a button styled only for text, so it inherits the global filled-button treatment | FE-002, FE-004 |
| Inputs show doubled/overlapping outlines with almost no vertical spacing | Raw auth `input` border/padding/height rules apply inside MUI OutlinedInput, alongside its own outline and wrapper `sx`; form layout has no consistent gap | FE-003, FE-004 |
| Placeholder text is almost invisible | `--text-placeholder: #d5d5d5`, compounded by MUI placeholder opacity, on a pale input surface | FE-001, FE-003 |
| Selected check mark has the wrong foreground | Global `span { color: ... }` overrides inherited foreground inside the selected button | FE-002, FE-004 |
| Buttons differ in height, radius, padding, and text size | Global rules, nav classes, page CSS, FormButton, MUI defaults, and a 900px breakpoint setting 28px button labels all compete | FE-002, FE-005 |
| Palette check passes while screens remain unreadable | `check-wcag.mjs` hardcodes stale colors and applies a 3:1 threshold to 14–16px button labels | FE-001, FE-008 |
| Layout spacing is fragile | App.tsx uses a fixed spacer and repeated `<br>` elements; mixed page widths and imperative nav class mutations | FE-005, FE-006 |

History identifies likely introduction points, not a proven single bad commit: `4686a520c` introduced the MUI FormInput wrapper while raw-input CSS remained; `e06921d04` introduced the S-070 palette/checker; `354ee6512` modified auth/nav styling and colors but left the conflicts above. Verify focused diffs before changing or reverting anything. Do not revert whole commits containing working functionality.

### Historical measured token pairs

Calculated from the initial audit CSS values. These are the historical failing pairs, not the current repaired palette; current source is covered by the FE validation records.

| Foreground / background | Ratio | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Gray `#555555` / action purple `#7d2ae8` | 1.20:1 | Fails text contrast; observed nav pairing |
| Auth-link `#9e9eff` / white | 2.39:1 | Fails small link text |
| Auth-link `#9e9eff` / action purple | 2.61:1 | Fails forgot-password text |
| Placeholder `#d5d5d5` / input `#f5f5f5` | 1.35:1 | Fails text contrast even before opacity |
| White / student green `#2e9e2e` | 3.47:1 | Fails 14–16px labels |
| White / error red `#e4394c` | 4.21:1 | Fails 14–16px labels |
| Input border `#c0c0c0` / input `#f5f5f5` | 1.67:1 | Insufficient if relied on to identify control boundary |
| White / action purple `#7d2ae8` | 6.23:1 | Suitable baseline for normal text |
| White / employer purple `#5d59ff` | 4.84:1 | Passes normal text; still check interaction states |

Use **4.5:1 for normal text**, including 14–16px bold button labels; 3:1 is allowed only for qualifying large text (at least 24 CSS px regular or about 18.67 CSS px bold). Necessary control/state indicators require 3:1 against adjacent colors. Disabled controls have WCAG exceptions but should still look intentional and readable. Check hover, selected, focus, loading, error, and images/overlays, not just token values.

References: [W3C text contrast](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html), [W3C non-text contrast](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-contrast.html).

- [x] Verification success gives a clear login continuation, and reset/signup password policy and confirmation errors agree with their shared validation rules and appear beside the relevant field.
- [x] All auth flows are visually checked in both roles and normal/loading/error/success states.
- [x] Frontend mandatory gates, contract/E2E checks for touched auth flows, contrast, and screenshots pass.

### SEC-004 — Fix rate limiting and password recovery

**Priority:** P1. **Audit:** Q-006.

- [x] REST and action routes share effective auth/verification limits that hold across concurrent Lambda instances.
- [x] Cleanup preserves the configured window; account and source attempt limits prevent challenge brute force.
- [x] Verification/reset challenges expire, are single-use, and have bounded attempts; resend behavior is defined.
- [x] Password reset revokes previous sessions and does not expose account existence unnecessarily.
- [x] Test expiry, exhaustion, replay, concurrency, cleanup, and both routing styles; mandatory gates pass.

**SEC-004 completion (30 October 2026; merged/deployed 31 October 2026):** implemented through a nine-stage adversarial tournament, merged to backend main during the all-branch integration and deployed. Rate limiting is now a persistent Postgres fixed-window bucket store with an atomic `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT` increment, injectable store (memory for unit tests), and named keys combining limiter, source (validated client IP) and account (SHA-256 of normalized email). Enforcement lives inside the auth/verification handlers, so action-style and REST dispatch share identical limits; `X-Forwarded-For` is trusted only behind an explicit proxy flag, and missing source IP skips the IP bucket instead of creating a global `unknown` bucket. Login 5/IP and 10/email, registration 3/IP and 3/email, reset send 3/IP and 3/email, verification 5/IP and 5/email per 15 minutes; cleanup is throttled per instance, bounded (10 x 500 rows), and deletes only `expires_at < now()` with an atomic recheck so active windows cannot be shortened.

Challenges: verification and reset codes expire after 10 minutes, are single-use via conditional updates inside the issuance transaction, and are cleared after 5 wrong attempts with atomic counter increments. Repeating registration for an existing unverified account reissues a code, invalidates the old one, preserves the attempt budget, and is rate-limited; new-account responses keep the `{student}`/`{employer}` public profile while resend responses are generic. Password reset increments `tokenVersion`, deletes all refresh tokens for the account in the same transaction, revokes stale access tokens, and always returns the same response regardless of account existence. Block/unblock and admin grant/revoke also revoke sessions transactionally under a shared admin lock, with a last-active-admin guard covering both demotion and block, idempotent no-op semantics, and audit entries only on real state changes. Advisory locks use a 63-bit namespace plus a legacy two-int bridge during rolling deploys.

Evidence: `pnpm check` exit 0 on final commit `806cc23` — 90 Vitest files / 447 tests, 5 scraper tests, 10 gate tests, typecheck, format, lint and build. Frontend `yarn check` (298 unit + 10 gate) and mobile `yarn check` (60 unit + 10 gate) pass on unchanged client source. Secret scan of tracked files and changed range clean. Tournament record (captains, judges, scores, losses) in `<workspace>/killer.json`; halt threshold (14 losses) never reached (9). Remaining limitations: no production load test or rate-limit drill was performed after deployment; refresh tokens are revoked transactionally rather than rotated, cleanup depends on traffic or the in-process timer, and access-token revocation for accounts blocked before this change depends on their prior `tokenVersion`.

### SEC-005 — Complete session lifecycle and refresh behavior

**Recheck — 1 November 2026: REOPENED (RCH-002/RCH-003).** A real-dispatch database probe finds the plaintext mobile refresh token in the generic idempotency response cache. Browser login replay also loses its refresh cookie. The token-table hashing/rotation work is present, but the end-to-end at-rest/session claim does not hold.

**Priority:** P1. **Audit:** Q-007.

**Historical logout gap (resolved):** frontend logout formerly cleared only local state and the backend lacked server revocation. SEC-005 added real logout and rotation/revocation; RCH-002/003 then repaired replay-cache and cookie behavior. Current implementation and verification are recorded below.

- [x] Session-store refresh secrets are hashed, rotated atomically and protected against reuse; required idempotency replay credentials are encrypted with a server-derived key; browser JSON omits cookie-only refresh credentials.
- [x] Logout revokes the server session and clears the cookie using matching attributes.
- [x] Invalid/expired tokens return consistent 401 responses; blocked-account/admin revocation delay is defined and enforced.
- [x] Refresh uses an isolated client/path that cannot queue behind itself; concurrent refresh and rejected refresh terminate reliably.
- [x] Test logout, expiration, reset revocation, reuse, blocking, concurrency, and refresh failure in both clients; mandatory gates pass.

**SEC-005 completion (31 October 2026):** implemented, validated, merged to main in backend, frontend and mobile during the all-branch integration and deployed. Refresh tokens are stored only as SHA-256 hashes with a family id, rotation timestamp and replaced-by hash. Refresh runs in one transaction: it locks the account and token row, rejects expired/revoked/unknown tokens with a stable 401, rotates the token in-family on success, and revokes the whole family when an already-rotated token is replayed. Login, registration verification, password-reset verification and refresh all set the HttpOnly `refreshToken` cookie (`Secure; SameSite=None; Path=/`); browser requests (Origin/Referer or `X-Client-Type: browser`) get no refresh token in JSON, while mobile still receives it. `POST /auth/logout` and action `log-out` accept the cookie or body token, delete its family and clear the cookie with matching attributes, idempotently. Logout is wired into the web navigation and the mobile sign-out path, and both clear local auth even if the request fails. Access tokens carry `tokenVersion`, checked per request, so block/admin revocation applies immediately to authenticated calls; refresh refuses revoked sessions. The web refresh call uses a dedicated axios client without app interceptors, and the mobile refresh path is excluded from interceptor retry.

Evidence: backend `pnpm check` exit 0 (91 files / 456 tests, 5 scraper, 10 gate; typecheck, format, lint, build); frontend `yarn check` (59 files / 302 tests + 16 gate); mobile `yarn check` (11 suites / 64 tests + 16 gate). Secret scans clean on all three branches. Branches `SEC-005-session-lifecycle`: backend `e29377e`, frontend `aa91dad`, mobile `543a495`. Limitations: concurrent refresh intentionally revokes the family (one winner, remaining 401), legacy plaintext refresh rows become unusable by design, logout is best-effort on the client, and no live browser/device validation was performed.

**3 November reconciliation:** RCH-002/003/009/011 repaired the cache/cookie/fingerprint/uncertain-outcome gaps and are ancestors of current backend main. The old confirmed-gap paragraph is historical: real logout/revocation now exists. The response cache uses encryption rather than claiming replayable credentials can be stored only as hashes.

**Priority:** P1. **Audit:** Q-013.

- [x] Database connections validate the proper certificate chain; untrusted certificates fail.
- [x] Missing secrets fail clearly; warm instances recover from credential rotation through bounded refresh/reconnect behavior.
- [x] Integration tests cover rotation with cached connections and failed refresh; no secrets appear in diagnostics.
- [x] Mandatory backend/rotation-package/infrastructure checks pass before push.

**SEC-006 completion (31 October 2026; backend merged/deployed, infrastructure merged but not applied):** implemented and validated. Backend TLS/retry changes are live; the rotation-Lambda infrastructure commit `a8abb7f` is on infrastructure main under `04d63bb` but the reviewed Terraform plan has not been applied. Lambda DB connections now use `rejectUnauthorized: true` with the RDS CA from `APP_DATABASE_CA` or `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` and fail closed if neither is configured; local development remains non-TLS. Tests prove a self-signed chain is rejected and the matching CA is accepted, and the adapter wiring is asserted. Secrets loading has a 5-minute TTL, single-flight, force reload, explicit fallbacks and clear missing-secret errors (no empty strings). `refreshDatabaseUrl()` rebuilds `DATABASE_URL` from freshly loaded secrets; `resetPrisma()` disconnects and clears the singleton; the Lambda entrypoint retries exactly once on credential errors (P1000/P1010/password authentication failed) after forcing refresh + reset, returns a generic 503 if recovery fails, and never retries other errors. Tests cover cached-connection rotation and failed refresh without leaking secrets.

The rotation Lambda now validates the RDS certificate chain using the bundled AWS RDS global CA (`rotation-function/global-bundle.pem`), with hostname checking and `CERT_REQUIRED`, fails clearly if the CA is missing, and the zip is rebuilt with the bundle. Evidence: backend `pnpm check` exit 0 — 96 files / 479 tests, 5 scraper, 10 gate; rotation Python tests 10/10; `terraform fmt -check` and `terraform validate` pass; secret scans clean. Branches `SEC-006-db-tls-rotation`: backend `21f6ed9`, infrastructure `a8abb7f`. Limitations: no live RDS TLS handshake or live rotation drill; the CA bundle is fetched from AWS without a pinned checksum; proactive refresh relies on TTL/credential-error recovery rather than a scheduled task.

- [x] Remove HTTP-triggered DDL and silent SQL-error swallowing; runtime DB role cannot modify schema.

- [x] Remove destructive local fallback and `.env` overwrite from test helpers.
- [x] Record recovery/rollback steps; mandatory backend/migration/infrastructure gates pass.

**REL-001 completion (31 October 2026):** implemented, validated, pushed (backend `0c156c6`, infrastructure `7e61514`) and executed against the live `dev` database on 31 October 2026. Removed the HTTP-triggered DDL path: deleted `pushSchema.ts` and its swallowed-error SQL executor, the `push-schema.sql` concatenation script, and the `seedDatabase` DDL call; seeding is DML-only and admin-gated. Added a transactional migration runner (`studup-db-migrator` Lambda, nodejs26.x, VPC) that uses master credentials from Secrets Manager with verified TLS, serializes on a Postgres advisory lock, maintains Prisma-compatible `_prisma_migrations` rows, verifies checksums, applies each migration in its own transaction, and supports an explicit snapshot-backed baseline (`BASELINE_MIGRATIONS` + `BASELINE_CONFIRM_DATABASE`) for a schema that predates the table. A `bootstrap-app-role` mode creates `studup_app` with DML/sequence/function privileges and default privileges while revoking CREATE; Terraform creates the app-role secret, the migrator role/policy/log group/VPC placement, and switches DataHandler to `APP_DATABASE_USER=studup_app` with `APP_DATABASE_SECRET_ID`. The backend CI `migrate` job builds/uploads the runner, invokes migrate then bootstrap, and fails the workflow; `deploy` now needs `[validate, migrate]`. README documents snapshot/backup, failure handling, baseline, app-role recovery and rollback.

Evidence: backend `pnpm check` exit 0 (105 files / 557 tests) including prefix-baseline and non-prefix rejection tests; infrastructure `npm run check` exit 0. Live execution (31 October 2026): created snapshot `studup-rel001-pre-202610311612` (status available), applied only the 9 REL-001 resources (0 change/0 destroy), inspected the live schema (no `_prisma_migrations`, 16 tables, identical column/index/enum sets to the first 15 packaged migrations), baselined that ordered prefix, applied the remaining 6 migrations, and bootstrapped `studup_app`. Final live schema matches a fresh full migration run (190 domain columns, 61 indexes; no missing/extra). The app role connects over verified TLS, has SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE but no CREATE/TRUNCATE (`permission denied for schema main`), and a repeat migrate is a no-op. The DataHandler environment switch was **not** deployed; it remains part of the unreviewed 56-add plan and should be applied with the normal release. Rollback is snapshot-based because there are no down migrations. DataHandler env is no longer in `ignore_changes`, so CI must not own its environment variables.

## Epic I — test types that provide missing evidence

**Recommendation:** keep Vitest for web/backend, Jest + React Native Testing Library for mobile, Playwright for web, Maestro for native, and k6 for load. Do not replace tools merely to get a higher test count. Improve what they exercise. Snapshot/render-string checks cannot prove successful login, native layout, database invariants, or authorization.

| Test layer | What it must prove | Normal execution point |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unit / boundary tests | Validation, transforms, status transitions, date/time and retry logic | Every affected push |
| Component interactions | Enter input, submit, await UI state, assert error/loading/navigation | Every affected push |
| API contract / handler dispatch | Real client payloads and real handler responses/routes agree | Every API/shared/client push |
| PostgreSQL integration | Migrations, constraints, authorization queries, transactions/concurrency | Every backend/data push |
| Browser/native E2E | A few complete student/employer journeys on isolated services | Relevant push/release gate; document any platform-specific cadence |
| Accessibility / visual | Computed contrast, keyboard/screen reader, responsive/native layout | Every affected UI push |
| Security regression | Cross-account access, leaked fields, token lifecycle, abuse limits | Every affected auth/data push |
| Resilience / load | Timeouts, provider failure, rotation, queue retry, saturation | Relevant architecture/release changes against an isolated environment |

## Runtime inspection — mobile app launched on this Mac

Performed 20 October 2026. **Target actually inspected: Expo web running the mobile source at `http://localhost:8082`, 1280×720. This is not native iOS/Android verification and not a phone-sized viewport.**

### Environment and scope

- The configured Xcode tree has no `Contents/Developer/Applications/Simulator.app`; the Simulator app could not be opened. Apple simulator/device discovery did not respond even outside the sandbox and was stopped. A simulator volume exists, so this is not evidence that all iOS runtimes are absent.
- No `adb` executable was available. No usable connected native device was established in this run.
- The first Expo web bundle failed because Zustand traditional imports `use-sync-external-store`, which mobile had not declared.
- After installing the missing peer, the bundle loaded but displayed a white screen. Browser layout inspection showed the root using a row: the full-width header occupied the viewport and the navigation sibling had width **0**, positioned at x=1280.
- Added an app-owned flex-column root View. Login and student/employer registration and password recovery then rendered and could be navigated.
- No accounts were created, credentials entered, password reset emails sent, or jobs/applications changed. Authenticated screens remain uninspected. Startup codebook requests failed; this run does not establish whether the cause is endpoint contract, CORS, service availability, or another network condition.

### Small fixes made to enable inspection

- `student-employer-mobile/package.json` / `yarn.lock`: added `use-sync-external-store` and its types; resolved runtime package 1.7.0. Applied package formatting to pass lint.
- `student-employer-mobile/App.tsx`: wrapped header/navigation in a `View` with flex:1 instead of rendering siblings directly into the web root.
- These changes are local, uncommitted, and unpushed. They do not complete the native build/device acceptance criteria.

Validation after the enabling fixes: `yarn typecheck` passed; `yarn lint` passed after package formatting; `yarn test --runInBand` passed **51 tests / 7 suites**; `expo export --platform web` passed. `expo export --platform all` failed at the Android bundle on missing `buffer` in the legacy AppSync dependency path. Native compilation/installation and iOS export were not established by that failed multi-platform run. Nothing was pushed because the native build gate is unresolved.

## Suggested order

1. CG-001, DEP-001, urgent SEC-001–SEC-003, and BE-001 containment; establish trustworthy dependencies and test fixtures before treating green checks as evidence.
2. Capture FE-000/MOB-000 baselines; repair immediate mobile toolchain mismatches through DEP-002, without forcing a discretionary SDK upgrade.
3. FE-001–FE-005 plus FE-008 and MOB-001–MOB-003 for visible usability; API-001–API-003 for working user flows.
4. Remaining security/backend/data/migration/release stories; TEST-002–TEST-006 are developed alongside the relevant fixes rather than deferred to the end.
5. FE-006–FE-007, mobile offline/media/release work, operations/docs/privacy, and selected product features. Schedule DEP-003 and discretionary major upgrades separately.

Do not add a monorepo migration, replacement CSS framework, microservices, staging stack, CAPTCHA, or extra AWS capacity simply to satisfy a generic best-practice label. Earlier declined choices remain declined unless the owner revisits them. Solve the measured defect first.

## RCH-010 — P1: make new-job watchlist matching recoverable

Further source review found that `createJob` commits the job and then calls `matchJobAlerts` with a catch-and-log fallback. The push worker can recover already-enqueued notifications, but it cannot recover an alert match that never ran or failed before creating those notifications. This leaves a crash/failure window where a published job never reaches matching students. The fault-injection regression reproduced this gap; the completed repair and evidence are recorded below.

Acceptance criteria:

- [x] Job creation and durable alert-matching intent commit atomically; matching failure does not lose the event or force a caller to recreate the job.
- [x] An independent worker retries matching after a later run without API traffic; duplicate/replayed delivery creates at most one inbox notification and push outbox record per job/student.
- [x] Preserve category, minimum-rate, employer/title filters, active subscriptions, privacy and job destinations; specify snapshot and unsubscribe behavior.
- [x] Cover a failure after job commit, later worker recovery, transaction rollback, overlapping matching attempts and a nonmatching/disabled watchlist.
- [x] Full typecheck, lint/format, build, tests, secret scan and exact-commit CI/deployment checks pass before completion.

Status: DONE — backend main `a1fd3bd`; Actions 41396409277 validate/build/migrate/deploy/smoke passed. 615 tests, 5 scraper tests, 16 gate tests, full quality checks and fresh 23-migration replay passed. Job plus durable matching intent commit atomically; bounded, resumable matching is independently retried with per-job/student deduplication. Snapshot/unsubscribe behavior is documented in `RCH010_WATCHLIST_RECOVERY.md`. Evidence: `recheck-fixes-2026-11-01/RCH-010/`.

## RCH-011 — P1: do not blindly rerun an uncertain committed mutation

The broader review found another idempotency gap: `runIdempotentMutation` can lose its response-cache write after the domain commit, while a stale PROCESSING lease is deleted after 60 seconds. A retry may then execute the mutation again. Generic 5xx cleanup also releases a key without proving the handler made no committed change. Fault injection reproduced this gap and the repair is complete; acceptance and evidence are recorded below. This supersedes the earlier claim that stale-lease takeover alone provided safe recovery.

Acceptance criteria:

- [x] A server interruption/cache-write failure after commit cannot automatically repeat the domain mutation within the documented idempotency window.
- [x] Represent uncertain outcomes durably; return useful reconciliation feedback, without replaying a stale transient 5xx or telling clients to blindly recreate an operation.
- [x] Allow automatic retry only for a trusted failure known to occur before domain execution. Preserve successful replay, body conflicts, encrypted cookies and bounded retention.
- [x] Test a post-commit cache failure, stale PROCESSING retry, 5xx after a committed write, safe pre-intent failure and a lost acknowledgement after a completed cache write.
- [x] Fresh Prisma migration replay, full checks and exact-commit CI/deployment pass before completion.

Status: DONE — backend main `88bc4f6`; Actions 41398744613 validate/build/migrate/deploy/smoke passed. 624 tests, 5 scraper tests, 16 gate tests and fresh 24-migration replay passed. ## RCH-012 — P1: safe push transports and subscription ownership

Further push-path review found: Expo/Web Push calls have no explicit delivery deadline; a missing Expo ticket is treated as success; Expo `InvalidCredentials` is classified as a bad device token; web-push registration accepts arbitrary URLs; and cross-account web subscription transfer does not verify existing key capability. Correction after source recheck: Context supplies null for the opposite role, so the old claim about undefined leaving both owners was inaccurate. The schema still lacks an exactly-one-owner constraint. Native delivery and both unregistration handlers are student-only despite employer registration support. Synthetic regressions reproduced the provider/registration gaps; the completed repair and evidence are recorded below. No internal/third-party endpoints or real device credentials were probed.

Acceptance criteria:

- [x] Provider timeouts/malformed or missing tickets remain retryable failures; server credential failures never delete valid device registrations. Verify provider batch limits against primary documentation.
- [x] Bound individual transport and overall worker time so hanging providers cannot monopolize an invocation; preserve existing retry/dead-letter behavior and invalid-registration cleanup.
- [x] Validate Web Push endpoints against approved HTTPS browser-push providers at registration and dispatch, including legacy rows; reject credentials, nonstandard ports and arbitrary/private destinations before networking.
- [x] Registration and schema enforce exactly one owner; cross-role/account transfer requires proof of the existing subscription capability and explicitly clears the previous owner. Quarantine or invalidate ambiguous legacy subscriptions without guessing a recipient.
- [x] Support employer native delivery and owner-scoped unregistration on both channels. Validate subscription key material, return minimal registration acknowledgements, and use configured support contact/current VAPID keys instead of hardcoded personal contact/stale initialization.
- [x] Add synthetic timeout, missing-ticket, InvalidCredentials, unsafe-URL, ownership-transfer and legacy-row tests. Full checks, fresh migrations, CI/deployment and live operational smoke must pass.

Status: DONE — backend main `f9996f8`; Actions 41404362924 validate/build/migrate/deploy/smoke and secret scan 41404362760 pass. Full local and pre-push gates passed 644 tests, 5 scraper tests, 16 gate tests; all 25 migrations replayed on a fresh local database. Ten-second bounded provider transport, overall elapsed worker budget, endpoint/key validation, capability-checked ownership transfer, database constraints, employer native delivery and safe cleanup are verified synthetically. Notes: `RCH012_PUSH_SAFETY.md`. Evidence: `recheck-fixes-2026-11-01/RCH-012/`. Provider acceptance does not prove device delivery; signed-device acceptance remains open.

## RCH-016 — P1: safe push diagnostics and native registration acknowledgements

Native HTTP diagnostics include the concrete request path. Unregister-device-token paths embed a provider token, and browser unregistration paths can embed a private push endpoint. Reproduce with synthetic identifiers; never print or send real tokens in regression evidence.

- [x] Test failed unregistration with synthetic native/web capabilities and assert logs contain the route template but no capability.
- [x] Sanitize local native review text artifacts that captured SDK-generated push tokens; retain screenshots and useful metadata.
- [x] Run all affected client quality gates and exact-commit CI before completion.
